original.description: The subject of this procurement proposal is the procurement of "Operations Engineering Services in support in ESEC/Redu" covering operational services for the preparation and execution of the mission operations entrusted to the Directorate of Operations located in ESEC, including the relevant Galileo Hosting Agreements.  ESA/ESEC is the ESA European Space Security and Education Centre located in Belgium and is one of the ESA sites in Europe. The main core business in Mission Operations relevant to this procurement are:  Control dedicated Satellites and Ground Segment (so called "Small Satellite missions")  Perform its In-Orbit activities.  Host and operate some ground segment elements in support to the EU Space Programme within a secured environment - mainly Galileo and EGNOS The Operational services, within the scope specified above, will be therefore divided in two main WPs: WP-1 Small Satellites Operations:   A number of Small Satellites (such as the PROBA ones) are or will be controlled from ESEC with the help of a dedicated ground segment. In the current set-up and number of missions, up to six passes per satellite daily are supported in automatic mode for TM reception and commanding, which may be extended in the future when new missions will be operated from ESEC. The mission products are made available at ESEC and ready for distribution. The Small Satellites Mission Operations Centre is therefore responsible of the monitoring and control of the satellite and the corresponding ground segment, the handling of the user requests, the extraction of the mission products and their availability for distribution.  The Small Satellites operations concept relies on a highly automatic functioning of the ground segment and a high degree of autonomy in the space segment for the delayed execution of operations requested by telecommand and for satellite survival. No operator attended shift work is foreseen. Operational engineers supervise the small satellites mission operations and related performances usually only during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The satellites are safe by design and can survive for a long period without ground station contact.   This WP will cover OPSPREP and OPS activities, support to Industry, execution of delegated tasks for critical operations (LEOP, others) together and in collaboration with Industry for this small satellite missions. This WP may implement further mission operations engineering activities carried out in support of other ESA programmes requested by ESA programme directorates to OPS. WP-2 Galileo Hosting activities:  The Galileo Hosting support will be provided in response to the requirements and agreements reached with EUSPA for Galileo and EGNOS. The provision of support to the hosting and testing activities will be performed on-site during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The Agency will issue one single Invitation to Tender in Open Competition for the two WPs. Considering the relatively small volume covered by this procurement, the Tenderers will be invited to provide a single proposal covering the support to both areas.   The new contract is planned to be kicked-off starting in 1st Quarter 2027 (phase-in) as required to permit sufficient time for a smooth transition (e.g. training, certification of new service provider's personnel).  The operational phase of the contract is expected to start latest by 2nd Quarter 2027, at the expiry of the current INDUSTRIAL SERVICE PROVISION IN SUPPORT OF THE OPERATION OF ESA IN BELGIUM contract extension.

original.description: Water Resources Management (WRM) and Disaster Risk Management (DRM) are two thematic areas that are important in Slovenia. In 2025 a preparatory activity concerning the contribution of satellite data for different thematic areas has highlighted the needs of priorities of a group of nationally mandated stakeholders from both the WRM sector and the DRM sector. While the ESA Digital Twin Earth (ESA DTE) programme is looking at integrating Earth Observation (EO) satellite capabilities in future operational Digital Twins ecosystems, including the potential future evolution of DestinE and other operational DT initiatives in Europe, this activity is a precursor development under the FutureEO programme to prepare the ground for an EO based digital ecosystem and connect EO data, processingchains and modelling. This FutureEO activity aims to implement and demonstrate a preliminary Digital Twin Precursor to prefigure potential EO based Digital Twin developments. original.description: ESA intends to implement a Zero Debris policy by 2030 and has a long-term vision for a sustainable and safe space environment leveraging on the development of a space circular economy.Large Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites in particular present significant risks, both in terms of potential collisions and ground casualty hazards resulting from uncontrolled re-entry.  The ESA's Clean Space Office has been pioneering the study of ADR since 2012, starting with the e.Deorbit study, followed by the ClearSpace-1 and the CAT mission in more recent years, under the ADRIOS initiative part of the ESA Space Safety Program. In the past years there has been growing interest in ADR services targeting large LEO debris objects. This topic has recently been the focus of discussions and studies between ESA and external stakeholders, including EUMETSAT in the frame of a feasibility study (e.g. CDF) and the European Commission(EC) via its ISOS framework. This led to the implementation of industrial activities for a 6 month ERASE phase 0 mission and systemstudy which was kicked-off Q1 of 2026.The activity proposed here is to further mature the concept of the ERASE mission up to the Preliminary Requirement Review (PRR) milestone. The result of the activity and the maturation of the ERASE concept should be in linewith the outcomes of an ESA Preliminary Requirements Review as described by the ECSS. If successful, ESA intends to follow this study by the  Phase B1 and a eventual full mission implementation acceptance after CMin 2028

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a wideband analogue beamforming integrated circuit (BFIC) capable of covering the entire frequency range from Cto Q/V-band, with two beams. This BFIC will serve as a modular and scalable solution for user-terminal flat-panel arrays, enabling multi-band and multi-product compatibility.Targeted Improvements: - Frequency coverage extended from C-band to Q/V-band in a single BFIC.- Fostering high-volume production scalability and economies of scale.- Enhanced design modularity, enabling flat-panel antennas to scale in aperture size (same number of beams) and/or number of beams (same aperture).Description:Conventionally, different BFICs have been used in applications at different frequency bands, e.g., the C- to Q/V-bands relevant to satcom. Also, such conventional BFICs typically generate a single beam. To enable the use of thesame BFIC in a broad range of satcom products, this activity will develop a next-generation dual-beam analogue BFIC with wideband coverage from C- to Q/V-band. Thus, the envisioned BFIC will serve as a fundamental building block for future flat-panel antenna arrays, supporting scalable designs by allowing additional BFICs to be integrated based on performance requirements. The development of this BFIC shall leverage insights from recent state-of-the-art wideband single-/dual-beam BFICs, such as the C- to Ka-band BFICs, which are developed outside ESA Member States. These contributions highlight the growing industry demand for multi-beam and frequency-agnostic BFIC solutions, which can reduce system complexity and accelerate product development, with the potential for higher volumeproduction in comparison to single-band BFICs. Therefore, the envisioned BFIC will cover the entire C- to Q/V-band range and generatetwo beams, which will enable its reuse across multiple product lines and reduce the need for band-specific BFICs. The design willemphasise performance consistency across the wide frequency range, minimising variations in gain, noise figure, and linearity.Additionally, the activity will assess the thermal and power consumption challenges associated with multi-beam and broadband analogue BFICs at millimetre-wave frequencies, ensuring that the proposed solution is viable for both low- and high-end satcom applications. Successful execution will position Europe as a leader in wideband BFICs, securing our competitiveness in the evolving satcom ecosystem. The wideband analogue BFIC will be tested against DVB-S2/S2X or 5G-NR waveform in a relevant environment.
